newsitem.title: USA: ATHLETICS-CHANGING OF THE GUARD IN U.S. SPRINTING.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-CHANGING OF THE GUARD IN U.S. SPRINTING.

text.p: Maurice Greene and Marion Jones, two up-and-coming speedsters, raced to the forefront of American sprinting with impressive 100-meter victories at the U.S. athletics championships on Friday.
Greene clocked 9.90 seconds to edge fellow 22-year-old Tim Montgomery by 0.02 seconds in a changing of the guard of U.S. sprinters.
Mike Marsh, the 1992 Olympic 200-meter champion, earned the final U.S. 100-meter berth for August's world championships in 10.03 seconds. He beat Jon Drummond by four-thousandths of a second.
Former world record-holder Leroy Burrell finished sixth in 10.09.
Only six men have ever run faster than Greene, a member of the 1995 U.S. world championship team who was injured last year.
"It's a great feeling," Greene said. "Last year was disappointing, but I knew if I trained the right way, my time would come."

The 21-year-old Jones, a teenaged sprint star who has concentrated on basketball in recent years, won the women's crown in 10.97 seconds to complete two days of sensational sprinting. She had clocked 10.98 and 10.92 seconds, the year's two fastest times, in Thursday's preliminaries.
"I'm exceptionally excited," said Jones. "After breaking my foot twice last year, I feel like I'm just now getting back to that world-class level that I first showed signs of in high school."

Two-time Olympic champion Gail Devers did not run because of what meet officials said was a sore right calf. But her coach, Bob Kersee, had threatened earlier to pull her from the race to express his displeasure at a move to grant world championship wild card spots to Olympic and world champions Michael Johnson and Dan O'Brien. The two are not competing here because of injuries.
Olympic champions Allen Johnson and Kenny Harrison won titles in contrasting styles.
Johnson led from the start in the 110-meter hurdles, winning in 13.25 seconds. Collegian Reggie Torian claimed silver in 13.28 seconds.
Harrison needed his final jump to become the triple jump champion at 16.97 meters (55 feet, 8 1/4 inches). LaMark Carter finished second at 16.76 (55 feet).
Antonio Pettigrew, the 1991 world champion, and world record-holder Butch Reynolds dominated the 400-meter semifinals. Pettigrew clocked 44.60 seconds and Reynolds ran 44.83.
Jearl Miles-Clark produced the year's fastest women's 400 meters, clocking 50.48 seconds in her semifinal.

Controversy was avoided in the men's 400-meter hurdles preliminaries when the IAAF waived its "contamination" rule, allowing suspended runner Stephon Flenoy to compete without danger of sanctions against the other hurdlers.
Flenoy, suspended after a positive drug test but competing after winning an arbitration hearing earlier in the week, finished last in his race and did not advance.
If the IAAF had not waived the rule, competitors in the race could have been suspended by the world governing body for running against an ineligble athlete.
